displayName: Legal Notice under Section 138 NI Act (Cheque Bounce)

mandatoryClauses.name: Cheque Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Cheque number, date, amount, bank name, branch

mandatoryClauses.name: Dishonour Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Date of dishonour, reason for dishonour (e.g., insufficient funds), bank memo reference

mandatoryClauses.name: Underlying Liability
mandatoryClauses.description: Nature of the legally enforceable debt or liability for which cheque was issued

mandatoryClauses.name: 15-Day Demand
mandatoryClauses.description: Demand to pay the cheque amount within 15 days of receipt of notice

mandatoryClauses.name: Criminal Prosecution Warning
mandatoryClauses.description: Warning that failure to pay within 15 days will result in criminal complaint under S.138 NI Act

mandatoryClauses.name: Advocate Details
mandatoryClauses.description: Name and enrollment number of advocate

prayerTemplate:
You are hereby called upon and demanded to make the payment of Rs. {amount}/- ({amountInWords}) within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of receipt of this notice.

Please note that in the event of your failure to make the said payment within the stipulated period of 15 days, my client shall be constrained to file a Criminal Complaint against you under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 before the competent court, at your risk, cost, and consequences.

This notice is without prejudice to the rights of my client to initiate civil proceedings for recovery of the said amount along with interest, damages, and cost of litigation.
filingChecklist: Notice sent within 30 days of receiving information of dishonour
Notice sent by Registered Post AD / Speed Post AD
Copy of bank memo / return memo
Wait 15 days from receipt of notice before filing complaint
File complaint within 30 days after expiry of 15-day notice period

sections.description: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds
Power of court to try cases summarily

promptInstructions: Draft a Legal Notice under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
This is a mandatory demand notice before filing a criminal complaint for cheque bounce.
Clearly state ALL cheque details: cheque number, date, amount (in figures and words), drawn on which bank and branch.
State the underlying legally enforceable debt/liability for which the cheque was issued.
Mention the date the cheque was presented for encashment and the date it was dishonoured.
State the reason for dishonour as mentioned in the bank's return memo (e.g., 'insufficient funds', 'account closed').
Include a clear demand for payment of the full cheque amount within 15 days of receipt of notice.
Warn that failure to pay within 15 days will result in criminal prosecution under Section 138 NI Act.
Reference the statutory timeline: notice within 30 days of dishonour knowledge, 15-day notice period, complaint within 30 days after notice period.
Use firm but professional legal language.
Do NOT generate the advocate signature block — it is added programmatically.
